analysis.title: US: Blue Deluge, Red Lights, Green Shoots (for 2028)
key_insights: Democrats flipped control of Congress in the 2026 midterms, winning at least 35 projected House seats against the net three needed, and flipping at least seven Senate seats (ME, NC, TX, OH, SC, KS, IA) against the four they hoped for.

The report attributes Democratic gains in deep red states to a collapse of Trump's 2024 coalition and record midterm turnout among young, Black and Latino voters. Democrats also won gubernatorial races in at least 6 of 7 states.

Incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jefferies listed three priorities: easing the affordability crisis, reversing healthcare cuts, and accountability on corruption backed by subpoena power. The report says affordability depends on ending the Iran war and lowering tariffs.

Trump has vowed to be 'Mr. Veto' and the White House is likely to ignore subpoenas. The report expects protracted gridlock, with Democrats using must-pass appropriations bills as leverage against Trump's priorities.
The report expects a bigger fiscal deficit as the path of least resistance, because healthcare funding and higher defence spending are both likely to be approved. More tariffs are also expected.
Republicans could still pass a debt ceiling increase in the lame duck session to avert a standoff next year.

The report is cautiously optimistic on bipartisan deals, starting with permitting reform. Others it names are shipbuilding, critical minerals and tough-on-China bills, including chip export controls if these are not folded into this year's NDAA. It says passage depends on the Trump administration.
Jefferies has a comfortable majority, which the report says lets moderate centrists, including new red-state Democrats, set the agenda instead of the democratic socialists.
Defense Secretary Hegseth is the Democrats' top target and could exit as Rumsfeld did after the 2006 midterms, though the report says another attack on Iran may come first.
If chief of staff Susie Wiles steps down and her deputy Stephen Miller steps up, the report expects a more hardline approach. Other picks would signal a less hardline one.
Trump is expected to pursue legacy goals by executive action in foreign policy (N. Korea and Cuba, as well as Iran, Russia and China), trade and tariffs, immigration and AI.
The report says the AI and data centre backlash is just beginning. It cites a chart showing Texas with 27% of the estimated US planned data centre buildout by GW, and promises a future note.
risk_factors: Protracted gridlock over must-pass appropriations bills
A larger fiscal deficit from healthcare and defence spending
Debt ceiling standoff next year if not resolved in the lame duck session
Trump vetoes and executive action that bypass Congress
Staff turnover that brings a more hardline White House, for example Stephen Miller replacing Susie Wiles
Backlash against AI and data centre buildout, concentrated in Texas
charts_described: Chart shows Democrats flipping at least seven Senate seats, five of them in ruby-red states, plotted by Trump's 2024 margin of victory or loss by state, with Democrats also holding four seats.
Chart shows the share of planned US data centre buildout by GW by state, with Texas at 27%.
geopolitical: Iran war: the report says easing the affordability crisis hinges on its end, and Hegseth may order another attack on Iran before any exit
Trump foreign policy focus on N. Korea and Cuba alongside Iran, Russia and China
Tough-on-China bills including chip export controls, possibly via the NDAA defence bill
Tariffs: more are expected despite Democratic pressure to lower them

tension_points.bull_case: A comfortable Democratic House majority lets centrists set the agenda, which the report says could allow bipartisan bills on permitting reform, shipbuilding, critical minerals and China measures.
tension_points.bear_case: Trump's veto pledge, likely disregard of subpoenas and Democratic use of appropriations leverage point to protracted gridlock and a bigger fiscal deficit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The report says bipartisan deals depend on the Trump administration choosing to play ball.

theme_stances.key_argument: Democrats will use must-pass appropriations bills as leverage, producing protracted gridlock and a larger fiscal deficit.
theme_stances.evidence: Protracted gridlock, with Democrats wielding must-pass appropriations bills as leverage
